text:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache backing service error rate and CPU spike detected for shard group kv-shard-7. severity: SEV2. affected: hosted inference region-us-west-2. key metrics: cache_entries=18.9M (+6x), avg_batch_size=128 (+3x), p50_latency_tokens=220ms -> 480ms, 5xx_rate=4.8%

alex: oncall alex here, picking this up. seeing the same in grafana. heatmap shows sustained large batches and cache fill. are we seeing increased traffic from any customers?

mira: infra: no customer ramp in billing logs. looks like a cache missstorm where KV chunking combined with continuous batching is enlarging prefix caches and causing warmup thrash. also HPA is spinning up pods but pods never reach steady state because of cache rebuilds.

jon: paging: I got the pager. I'm seeing a correlation with a recent batch policy change rolled 2h ago (increase max_batch_size from 64 -> 256) in prod routing. could be the trigger.

sam: this matches the deploy audit. deploy-bot shows:
```
deploy-bot: rollout config: /configs/batching/prod.json changed by lucy@infra at 2026-03-15T10:12Z
- max_batch_size: 64 -> 256
- enable_prefix_cache_reuse: true
```

alex: ok. hypothesis: larger max_batch_size increased avg batch size which makes KV per-request footprint grow -> cache population explosion -> longer cold-starts -> HPA overshoots -> thrash. need immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact.

mira: possible mitigations in order: 1) revert batch config (fast but might require canary rollback), 2) change HPA thresholds to be less aggressive (cooldown), 3) temporary cache TTL reduction to avoid memory blowups.

jon: customer-impact? which routes/models are affected?

sam: tracing shows spike in model-serving route /v1/generate for model-rank: open-7b-quant at 88% of errors. customers with long-context requests see most errors, but error rate is small overall; however latency SLOs are violated for many paid users. recommend contacting success team.

alex: I'm going to open a short-lived mitigation: rollback max_batch_size to 64 for prod routing and set HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds to 90s (was 30s). can one of you apply the HPA patch?

mira: applying HPA patch now. kubectl patch:
```
kubectl -n inference patch hpa kv-serving-hpa -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":90},"scaleUp":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":90}}}}'
```

deploy-bot: NOTE: rolling back routing config requires a restart of the routing service to pick up config. two pods will bounce.

alex: jon, can you stage the config rollback and coordinate restart during low risk window (next immediate minutes)? I'll monitor.

jon: staging rollback now to canary. patch applied to canary routing group. observing canary traffic for 2 minutes.

sam: monitoring logs: avg_batch_size on canary dropped from 130 -> 58 within 40s. p50 latency for canary improved ~30%.

jon: starting roll to 10% prod groups. will watch HPA.

irene: heads-up: I'm on support rotation, have DMs open for customer comms; will prepare a short status blurb for customer success teams.

alex: HPA behavior looks calmer. overall cluster CPU starts trending down. cache_entries growth stopped on canary.

incident-bot: UPDATE: automated alert suppression enabled for this thread to reduce noise.

jon: rolling remaining traffic back now. schedule: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 2m windows.

mira: recommendation post-rollback: we should add a guard to the batching policy that enforces per-key rate limits for KV cache population, and a gradual ramp for max_batch_size (e.g., 64 -> 96 -> 128 over 24h with canaries). also add a quick mitigation option to cap batch size per model.

sam: patch complete. full rollback to 64 applied. doing post-rollback health checks.

alex: health checks: p50 latency returning to baseline, 5xx down to <0.3%, HPA pods stable (no thrash). looks good.

irene: customer comms draft: "We've identified a regression caused by a recent batching config change that temporarily increased latency and error rates for some long-context requests. We've rolled back the change and implemented HPA stabilization. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem." anyone want to edit?

jon: add ETA for postmortem in 48h and list impacted model(s).

mira: I'll follow up with an engineering action list: 1) add traffic-aware batching guard, 2) add per-model batch caps and ramping, 3) HPA tuning: longer stabilization and larger scaleDown cpu threshold margin, 4) write a chaos test for cache warmup.

alex: handing off to next on-call for monitoring and post-rollback watch. next-oncall: jon for remainder of day. I'm going offline in 10.

jon: taking over. I'll keep an eye for 2 hours and queue the rollback change for PM review. thanks.

sam: logging the incident: INC-2026-0315-KV-BATCH-01. brief notes saved in incidents channel.

irene: pinging success team: @customer-success please notify customers who saw degradation (I'll DM the list).

incident-bot: SEV2 -> mitigated. follow-up required: postmortem and configuration gating.

alex: quick nudge: let's add a playbook entry for "batching config rollback" with exact kubectl steps and whom to notify. saved to runbook.

mira: will create a PR with the batching guard and add config validation to CI to prevent large global increments without canary.

jon: last check: no new alerts for 12m. handing off full ownership to sam for postmortem drafting.

sam: noted. will produce postmortem with timeline, root cause, mitigations, and customer impact summary. aiming for first draft in 48 hours.

alex: thanks all. good ops. :thumbsup:
